newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC says launches world's thinnest television.
newsitem.headline: NEC says launches world's thinnest television.

text.p: Japanese electronics giant NEC Corp said on Thursday it had begun selling the world's thinnest television, with a picture quality matching that of ordinary TVs.

NEC is the second company after Fujitsu Ltd to market a 42-inch plasma display panel (PDP) -based television in Japan employing flat-panel technology which uses gas and electric charges to create full colour images.
"This is definitely the thinnest TV in the industry, with the highest picture quality," NEC president Hisashi Kaneko told a news conference.
The company said its new television, named Plasma X, measures 99 mm in width, including power supply, tuner and speakers.
Ordinary 42-inch TVs measure about one metre in width because they use bulky cathode-ray tubes.
"NEC believes the flat-panel will become the core technology for our multimedia business," Kaneko said.
Another NEC official said the company plans to make 10,000 42-inch Plasma X TV sets in the first year of production.
By 2000, NEC aims to capture 10 percent of Japan's PDP TV market, which it estimates at 1.8 million units.

Unlike cathode-ray tubes and liquid crystal displays, PDP technology allows for larger screens without an increase in weight or thickness, making it possible to create thin and lightweight televisions that can be hung on walls.
Liquid crystal display technology is also suited for space-saving TVs, but a complicated production process makes it difficult to produce LCD panels larger than 30 inches.
NEC said it has developed so-called "capsulated colour filter technology" to achieve a picture quality and clear colour contrast on a par with cathode-ray-tube televisions.
The colour filter technology cuts out unnecessary light as the plasma discharges to offer pure colours, NEC said.
Plasma X's can be used as monitors for personal computers and to receive high definition broadcasts, NEC said.
The new product, priced at 1.2 million yen ($9,900) in Japan, will also be sold abroad.
Kaneko said he expects the price of 42-inch PDP TVs to halve by 2000.
NEC said it plans to invest 85 billion yen ($702 million) in PDP production facilities by 2000.
Besides NEC and Fujitsu, Pioneer Electronic Corp, Mitsubishi Electric Corp and South Korea's Daewoo Corp, among others, are planning to invest heavily in PDP TV production.
Sony Corp produces a different type of PDP, using PALC (Plasma-addressed liquid crystal) technology. ($1=121 yen)
